resources.name: Central Texas Food Bank
resources.description: Get free groceries from many food pantries in Austin and nearby areas. They also help you apply for SNAP (food stamps) and other food help. You can search for pantries by your zip code on their website. Many sites are open on different days and times. Some places offer drive‑through food pick up. No one is turned away for the first visit, but bring an ID if you have one. Call or check online for a pantry close to 78702 and for current hours.

resources.name: Caritas of Austin – Food Services
resources.description: Get free groceries and help with meals if you are very low income or homeless. They offer a food pantry and other food help for people in Austin. Staff can also help you find other places for food and housing help. You may need to do a first visit and share some basic papers, like ID if you have it. Call first to learn who can get help and what to bring. This site is close to zip code 78702.

Ask about any limits on how often you can come.

resources.name: SAFE Alliance – SAFEline and Emergency Shelter
resources.description: Get safe shelter, help with safety planning, and support for adults and kids facing abuse. Staff can help with a protective order, court papers, and talking with police. They offer a safe place, food, clothing, and help finding longer term housing. They can also help with child care, school, and basic needs while you stay there. You can call, text, or chat any time, day or night. All help is private, and they will not share your story without your okay. You do not have to file a police report to get help here. They can also help if you are not a U.S. citizen.
resources.availability_status: Call SAFEline first for space and intake

resources.name: SAFE Alliance – Eloise House and Legal Help
resources.description: Get help with a protective order, legal options, and safety planning after abuse. Staff can explain court steps in simple words and help fill out forms. They can go with you to court if needed. You can also get a medical exam after sexual assault, even if you do not want police. All help is private and free. You can call the main SAFEline to reach the legal team. They can help even if you are still living with the person who hurt you. They can also help if you do not speak English well.
resources.address: 300 E Highland Mall Blvd, Suite 110, Austin, TX 78752
resources.availability_status: Call SAFEline to connect with legal team and set up a visit

resources.name: Texas Advocacy Project – Legal Line for Domestic Violence
resources.description: Get free legal help by phone for domestic violence, stalking, or sexual assault. Lawyers can help with protective orders, divorce, child custody, and safety plans. You can call from anywhere in Texas. They can help even if you do not have money for a lawyer. They can explain your rights in simple words. They can help you plan how to leave safely. They can also help if you are not a U.S. citizen. Calls are private, and they will not share your story without your okay.
resources.address: 4606 W Howard Ln, Suite 730, Austin, TX 78728
resources.availability_status: Phone line open weekdays; leave a message after hours

You may need a police report or other proof, but they can explain what papers you need. Help is for people who live in Travis County or were hurt in Travis County.
resources.availability_status: Open weekdays; call first to check hours or set a visit

Staff can explain your rights in simple words. They can also help if you speak Spanish or another language. Call first to apply and see if they can take your case.

Staff can also help with finding a lawyer, housing, and basic needs. Some staff speak Spanish and other languages. You do not have to live in their shelter to ask for legal help. Call first to learn if they can help and what papers you should bring.
resources.availability_status: Shelter often full; legal and rights help may still be open—call first

resources.name: Austin Community College – Adult Education (ESL and GED)
resources.description: Get free English classes and GED (high school equivalency) classes for adults. Classes are in many parts of Austin, some in person and some online. They have different levels, from beginner to advanced English. Staff can help you take a simple test to find your level. Classes are for people who are 18 or older and not in high school. You must sign up and go to an information meeting before classes start.
resources.availability_status: Classes follow school terms; some classes may have waitlists

resources.name: Literacy Coalition of Central Texas – English@Work and Adult English Classes
resources.description: Get free or low-cost English classes for adults who want to improve reading, writing, and speaking. Some classes are for workers at job sites. Other classes are open to the public at partner places. They also help people sign up for GED (high school equivalency) and job training. Staff can help you find a class near your home or bus line. Call or use the website form to learn about class times and how to sign up.
resources.address: 1111 W 6th St, Suite A-300, Austin, TX 78703
resources.availability_status: Class spots change often; call to check current openings

resources.name: ESL and Citizenship Program – Austin Public Library
resources.description: Get free English practice groups and help studying for United States citizenship at the library. Some branches offer small English groups with a leader. Others offer one-on-one practice with a tutor. They also have books and online tools to learn English. Help is for adults and does not check income or immigration status. Call or visit the website to see which branches near you have English groups now.
resources.address: 710 W César Chávez St, Austin, TX 78701
resources.availability_status: Schedules differ by branch; some groups may be full, so call ahead

resources.name: American Gateways – Austin
resources.description: Get low-cost or free help with immigration papers and learning your rights in the United States. Staff can explain your options for visas, green cards, or safety from harm. They also give short classes and talks about immigrant rights in simple language. You can ask questions in private. Some staff speak Spanish and other languages. You may need to share your income to see if you can get free help. Call first to learn how to sign up and what papers you need.
resources.address: 314 E Highland Mall Blvd, Suite 501, Austin, TX 78752
resources.availability_status: Call for current wait times; some programs may have a waitlist

resources.name: Catholic Charities of Central Texas – Immigration Legal Services
resources.description: Get help with immigration forms, green cards, citizenship, and learning your rights as an immigrant. Staff are trained in immigration law and can explain things in simple words. They offer low-cost help and sometimes free help for people with low income. They do not ask about religion for this help. You must call to set up a first visit. Ask what papers you need to bring and how much it may cost.
resources.availability_status: May have waitlist for new cases; call to check openings

Call first or use the website to ask for help and learn if they can take your case.

resources.name: CommUnityCare Health Centers – Dental
resources.description:
Get low-cost dental care if you have low income or no insurance. They can help with exams, cleanings, fillings, and pulling teeth. You pay on a pay what you can afford plan based on income. You may need to share pay stubs or other income papers. Call to ask about first visit, cost, and what papers you need. They can help in English and Spanish. Bus lines stop nearby.

You can get cheap dental help here if you do not have much money. They help with tooth pain, cleanings, and fixing teeth. How much you pay depends on what you earn. Bring pay stubs or income papers if you have them. Call first to set up a visit and ask what to bring.
resources.availability_status: Call for current openings; some clinics may have a waitlist
resources.source: Listed in provided references as CommUnityCare Health Centers – Dental; details verified on communitycaretx.org

resources.name: People's Community Clinic – Medical and Dental Partners
resources.description:
Get low-cost health care if you have low income or no insurance. They can help with check-ups, sick visits, and some basic dental help through partner dentists. They use a pay what you can afford plan based on income and family size. You may need to share ID and income papers. Call to ask about dental help, cost, and how to become a patient. Staff can help in English and Spanish.

You can get cheap doctor help here if you do not have insurance. They also work with dentists for basic tooth care. What you pay depends on what you earn. Call first to ask about dental spots and what papers to bring.
resources.availability_status: New patient spots may be limited; call to ask about wait time
resources.source: Listed in provided references as People's Community Clinic; details verified on peoplesclinic.org

resources.name: Integral Care – Health and Dental Help Connections
resources.description:
Get help finding low-cost health and dental care if you have low income. This group mainly helps with emotions and behavior, but staff can also help you find clinics that fit your budget. They can help you apply for Medicaid (free health care for low income) and other health plans. Call any time if you need help or feel very stressed. Ask to talk with someone about low-cost health or dental care.

You can call here to find cheap health and tooth care. They do not fix teeth, but they help you find a clinic. They can also help you apply for health plans like Medicaid. Call and say you need help finding low-cost dental care.
resources.availability_status: Phone line open 24/7; in-person visits may need a first visit
resources.source: Listed in provided references as Integral Care; details verified on integralcare.org

Help is for people with low income in Texas. You can call from anywhere in Austin.
resources.address: 1920 E Riverside Dr, Suite A-120, Austin, TX 78741
resources.availability_status: Call for current hours and to see if you qualify

resources.name: Texas RioGrande Legal Aid – Austin Office
resources.description: Get free legal help with money harm, family problems, and safety for people with low income. They can help older people facing financial harm by family, like stolen money or misuse of power of attorney. They may help with housing, benefits, and safety planning. You must meet income rules and live in their service area. Austin and Travis County are in their area.
resources.availability_status: Call for a phone evaluation and to check if they can take the case

resources.name: AGE of Central Texas – Caregiver and Senior Support
resources.description: Get help for older people and their helpers, like support, classes, and memory care day programs. Staff can help with safety planning, money harm concerns, and finding trusted local help. They offer support groups, help with choices, and links to legal and safety help. This group serves older adults and their families in Austin and Central Texas.
resources.availability_status: Some programs have wait lists; call to ask about openings

resources.name: Family Eldercare – Guardianship, Money Management, and Senior Support
resources.description: Get help to protect older people from money harm and unsafe living situations. They offer money management help, payee help for Social Security, and guardianship in some cases. Staff can help watch bills, protect income, and lower the risk of money harm by others. They also connect older people to housing, health, and safety help. Serves older adults and adults with disabilities in Central Texas.
resources.availability_status: Some programs may be full; call to learn about current openings

resources.name: Area Agency on Aging of the Capital Area (CAPCOG)
resources.description: Get help finding local support for older people, like legal help, safety, and money help. Staff can explain choices, help with benefits like Medicare, and connect you to trusted legal and elder abuse help. They serve people age 60 and older in Travis County and nearby counties. They can also talk with family or helpers if the older person agrees.
resources.address: 6800 Burleson Rd, Building 310, Suite 165, Austin, TX 78744
resources.availability_status: Call during weekday business hours

resources.name: Texas Health and Human Services – Office of the Ombudsman for Long-term Care and Elder Rights

resources.availability_status: Phone help during weekday business hours; voicemail after hours

resources.name: Texas Adult Protective Services (APS) – Abuse, Neglect, and Financial Exploitation Hotline
resources.description: Get help if someone is hurting, neglecting, or stealing money from an older or disabled person. You can report financial exploitation by a family member or anyone else. You can report for yourself or for someone you know. APS workers can check on safety, explain options, and help connect to other help. Reports can be private. This help is for people age 65 or older, or adults with disabilities.
resources.availability_status: 24/7 hotline – call any time, day or night
resources.source: Texas Department of Family and Protective Services official website

resources.name: Texas RioGrande Legal Aid – Austin
resources.description: Get free legal help with elder abuse, money problems, and safety for low income people. They can help with financial exploitation, power of attorney problems, and getting money or property back. They may also help with safety plans and protective orders. Help is for people with low income in their service area. There may be wait times, so call as soon as you can.
resources.availability_status: Call for current intake hours; phone lines can be busy
resources.source: Texas RioGrande Legal Aid official website

resources.name: Dispute Resolution Center of Travis County
resources.description: Get low cost or free help to talk through money and family conflicts with a neutral helper. This can help when an older person has money conflict with a family member. They do not give legal advice, but they help people talk and make agreements. Help is for people in Travis County. There may be a small fee, but they can lower it based on income.
resources.address: 5407 North Interstate Highway 35, Suite 410, Austin, TX 78723
resources.availability_status: Call to schedule; some help may be by phone or video
resources.source: Dispute Resolution Center of Travis County official website

resources.name: AGE of Central Texas – Caregiver and Older Adult Support
resources.description: Get help for older adults and their families, like support, classes, and day programs. They can give information on elder abuse, money safety, and planning. Staff can help explain options and connect you to legal and safety help. This group mainly serves older adults and family caregivers in Central Texas. Some programs are free, some have a fee.
resources.availability_status: Call for program openings and hours; some waitlists may exist
resources.source: AGE of Central Texas official website

resources.name: Area Agency on Aging of the Capital Area (AAACAP)
resources.description: Get free help for people age 60 and older, like benefits help and safety planning. They can help older adults who face abuse or money exploitation. Staff can explain rights, help with reporting, and connect to legal help. They also help with Medicare, long-term care, and support for people who live alone. This help is for older adults in Travis and nearby counties.
resources.address: 6800 Burleson Road, Building 310, Suite 165, Austin, TX 78744
resources.availability_status: Open weekdays; call first to talk with a staff person
resources.source: Area Agency on Aging of the Capital Area official website

resources.name: Texas Legal Services Center – Legal Hotline for Texans
resources.description: Get free legal advice by phone for people age 60 or older or on Medicare. Lawyers can explain rights after financial exploitation, debt, and money scams. They can help you understand papers you signed and what you can do next. This is a phone and online help line for people in Texas. They do not go to court in every case, but they give strong legal advice.
resources.availability_status: Open weekdays; call for current hours
resources.source: Texas Legal Services Center official website

resources.name: Family Eldercare – Financial and Aging Support
resources.description: Get help with money safety, payee help, and support for older adults who may be at risk. They can help protect money, pay bills safely, and plan for the future. They serve older adults and adults with disabilities in Central Texas.
